description: We are building a two-storey semi-detached house (side-by-side duplex) in Edmonton. Each half has a legal basement secondary suite, so four dwelling units in total. The building area is 180 m2. Stick-framed lumber rafters and ceiling joists from the Part 9 span tables (no roof trusses); floor joists span 4.3 m; plain concrete footings and foundation walls from the Section 9.15 tables; no sprinkler or fire alarm system; not on permafrost; the building official has not asked for professional drawings. The longest rafter is a 4.1 m clear span.
known_facts: two halves, each with a basement secondary suite

gold.engineering_reason: Code: 2 principal units (suites need not count, Div C 2.4.1.1.(2)) is within the 4-unit exception. Acts: 4 dwelling units even counting the suites, which is "4 dwelling units or less". Boundary case for the suite rule. No Part 9 to Part 4 trigger is stated: spans are at most 12.20 m and floor joists at most 4.9 m, live load is residential, Edmonton 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is 0.45 kPa (below 1.2) and Sa(0.2) is 0.103 (not above 1.2 or 1.8), no wood roof trusses, no sprinkler/alarm system, and no AHJ direction under Div C 2.4.1.1.(4).
gold.limit_source: Div A 1.3.3.3.(1) (Part 9 applies); Div C 2.4.1.1.(1) exception; Architects Act s.2(5)-(6) and EGPA s.2(6)-(7) exceptions; Part 4 triggers absent per Div B 9.23.1.1.(1), 9.15.3.3.(1), 9.23.3.5.(4), 9.23.6.1.(6), 9.23.16.5.(3); Div B Appendix C Tables C-2/C-3 (Edmonton).

authoring.notes: Constructed scenario, not a real case. Gold written from the quoted sources before any system run. Not human-reviewed. Boundary case: counting suites lands exactly on the Acts' 4-unit limit.

assumptions: No AHJ direction under Div C 2.4.1.1.(4) or Administrative Items Regulation s.18 (stated in the text as "has not asked for professional drawings").
Rafter and joist sizes taken from the Part 9 span tables (Div B 9.23.4.2.); table values not re-checked here.
